title: Linkability of Homeowner Data Across Systems
description: Data collected during account registration and device enrollment could be linked across different systems or services, potentially revealing the homeowner's identity and behavior patterns.
assumptions: Multiple data sources exist that could be correlated

title: Identification of Homeowner Through Account Registration
description: Personal information provided during account registration could be used to directly identify the homeowner, potentially exposing their identity to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: Account registration requires personally identifiable information

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Camera/Sensor Data
description: Video and sensor data collected from enrolled cameras and sensors could be disclosed to unauthorized third parties, potentially revealing private home activities and occupant information.
assumptions: Data is transmitted or stored in ways that could be intercepted

title: Undetected Unauthorized Access to Home Hub
description: Unauthorized access to the Home Hub could occur without detection, allowing attackers to access enrolled devices and collected data without the homeowner's knowledge.
assumptions: Access controls may have vulnerabilities or be bypassed

title: Usurpation of Homeowner Identity for Device Enrollment
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the homeowner to enroll unauthorized cameras or sensors, gaining access to the home network and data.
assumptions: Authentication mechanisms may be weak or bypassable

title: Guest Access Code Linked to Identity
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest user could be linked to their identity through system logs or metadata, potentially revealing patterns of guest visits and their association with the home.
assumptions: The system logs access attempts with user identification

title: Guest Identity Inferred from Access Code Entry
description: An observer could potentially identify the guest user by monitoring the access code entry process, especially if the code is visible or if the system displays user information upon entry.
assumptions: Access code entry is observable or user information is displayed

title: Access Code Disclosure to Unauthorized Parties
description: The temporary access code could be disclosed to unauthorized individuals through shoulder surfing, network interception, or improper logging of the code.
assumptions: Access code is transmitted or stored in a way that could be intercepted

title: Unauthorized Code Reuse or Sharing
description: The temporary access code could be shared with or reused by unauthorized persons, allowing them to gain access to the home without proper authentication.
assumptions: Guest may share code or code is not properly invalidated after use

title: Lack of Non-Repudiation for Access Events
description: The system may not provide adequate proof of who entered the access code, making it difficult to verify or dispute access events in case of security incidents.
assumptions: System does not maintain tamper-proof audit logs

title: Disclosure of household activity patterns
description: The local event log containing motion/door/sensor events could reveal sensitive information about household routines, presence patterns, and daily activities. This could enable stalking, burglary planning, or social engineering attacks against household members.

title: Linkability of events to individuals
description: Event log entries could be linked to specific individuals or activities, potentially revealing associations, relationships, or patterns of behavior that should remain private.

title: Tampering with event log integrity
description: An attacker with physical or digital access to the local event log could modify, delete, or inject false events, compromising the integrity of the security records and potentially enabling cover-up of malicious activities.

title: Identification of individuals from event metadata
description: The Home Hub process could inadvertently include identifying metadata (timestamps, device IDs, location data) in the event log that could be used to identify specific individuals or their presence at the location.

title: Unauthorized Access to Cloud-Stored Video Clips
description: Cloud video storage may be accessible by unauthorized parties, allowing them to view recorded camera footage without permission.
assumptions: Cloud storage provider has inadequate access controls or authentication mechanisms.

title: Data Breach of Video Content
description: Cloud video storage could be compromised through security vulnerabilities, leading to exposure of sensitive home surveillance footage.
assumptions: Cloud storage infrastructure has security vulnerabilities or is subject to attacks.

title: Identification of Individuals in Video Footage
description: Recorded camera clips may capture identifiable individuals (family members, visitors, neighbors) within the home environment.
assumptions: Video footage is clear enough to identify faces or distinguishing features.

title: Linkability of Video Clips to Specific Events
description: Video footage can be linked to specific times, locations, and activities, potentially revealing patterns of behavior or sensitive events.
assumptions: Metadata or timestamps in video files allow correlation with other data sources.

title: Tampering with Video Evidence
description: Cloud-stored video data could be altered, deleted, or corrupted, compromising the integrity of recorded evidence.
assumptions: Cloud storage lacks proper integrity controls or digital signatures.

title: Unauthorized Access to Home Hub Upload Function
description: An attacker could potentially gain control of the Home Hub and upload malicious or unauthorized video content to the cloud.
assumptions: Home Hub authentication is compromised or weak.

title: Linkability of Motion Alerts Across Time
description: Motion alerts forwarded from the Home Hub could be linked to specific users or locations over time, enabling the creation of movement profiles that reveal patterns of daily life.
assumptions: The system retains historical motion alert data and associates it with user accounts.

title: Inference of Occupancy Status
description: Real-time motion alerts could reveal when individuals are present or absent from the home, potentially identifying specific users based on movement patterns and timing.
assumptions: Motion detection is sensitive enough to distinguish between different occupants or infer presence/absence.

title: Unauthorized Disclosure of Motion Data
description: Motion alert data stored or processed by the Mobile App Backend could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through system vulnerabilities, insider threats, or inadequate access controls.
assumptions: The backend has access to motion data and may store it for analytics or other purposes.

title: Usurpation of Home Hub Identity
description: An attacker could potentially impersonate the Home Hub to send false motion alerts to the Mobile App Backend, or intercept legitimate alerts in transit.
assumptions: Communication between Home Hub and backend lacks strong authentication or encryption.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of motion detection data
description: Motion-detected notification could be intercepted or accessed by unauthorized parties, revealing the homeowner's presence at a location and potentially their daily routines or habits.
assumptions: Assumes notification transmission is not fully encrypted or is accessible to network attackers.

title: Linkability of motion data to other homeowner data
description: Motion detection notifications could be linked with other data about the homeowner (e.g., location history, access logs) to create a detailed profile of their behavior and presence patterns.
assumptions: Assumes other data flows exist that could be correlated with this notification data.

title: Excessive data collection in notification
description: Notification may contain more data than necessary (e.g., precise location, timestamp, motion type) which could be used to infer sensitive information about the homeowner's activities.
assumptions: Assumes notification payload includes detailed metadata beyond simple alert.

title: Linkability of Aggregated Analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics shared with cloud vendor may be linkable to specific users or devices through cross-referencing with other data sources, enabling potential re-identification.
assumptions: Cloud vendor has access to additional data sources that could be correlated with the analytics data.

title: Unauthorized Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Cloud analytics vendor may share or sell the aggregated analytics data to third parties without proper authorization or consent from the mobile app users.
assumptions: Cloud vendor has business incentives to monetize the analytics data beyond the agreed scope.

title: Inference of User Behavior Patterns
description: Even aggregated analytics may reveal sensitive user behavior patterns, preferences, or habits that could be inferred and potentially misused.
assumptions: Analytics data contains sufficient detail to enable behavioral inference about user groups or individuals.

title: Data Integrity Compromise During Transmission
description: Analytics data could be tampered with, altered, or corrupted during transmission between mobile app backend and cloud analytics vendor.
assumptions: Transmission channel is not fully secured or integrity verification mechanisms are insufficient.

title: Regulatory Non-Compliance with Privacy Laws
description: Cloud analytics vendor may not comply with applicable privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA) regarding data processing, storage, and user rights.
assumptions: Cloud vendor operates in multiple jurisdictions with varying privacy requirements and may not have adequate compliance measures.

title: Unauthorized Access to Stored Video Data
description: Cloud video storage may be accessible by unauthorized parties through security vulnerabilities, insider threats, or compromised credentials, leading to potential exposure of homeowner surveillance footage.

title: Identifiability of Individuals in Video Footage
description: Stored video clips may contain identifiable information about the homeowner, family members, visitors, or other individuals, potentially enabling identification and profiling.

title: Insecure Data Retrieval from Backend
description: Mobile app backend may retrieve video data without proper authentication or authorization checks, allowing unauthorized access to stored video clips.

title: Linkability of Video Data to Homeowner Identity
description: Video data retrieved by the backend may be linked to the homeowner's identity through metadata, access logs, or user profiles, enabling correlation of surveillance data with personal information.

title: Excessive Video Data Collection and Storage
description: The system may store video clips beyond what is necessary for the playback function, retaining more data than required and increasing privacy exposure.
